articleTitle: Reflection of an open-ended coaxial line and application to nondestructive measurement of materials
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: With the appearance of low-cost solid-state sources, microwaves provide an interesting tool for the nondestructive testing of various materials, among others, in the field of biomedicai engineering. Reflection measurement techniques require a way to correlate measured reflection factors with the permittivity of the material. This relationship is derived here for the open-ended coaxial line propagating the TEM mode.

articleTitle: On the signal-to-noise ratio and short-term stability of passive rubidium frequency standards
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Results are presented on theoretical calculations of the signal-to-noise ratio and of the short-term stability realizable in passive rubidium frequency standards. Measurements made on systems using either the separate hyperfine filter or the integrated hyperfine filter approach are reported. It is concluded that shot noise produced by the lamp at the photodetector is responsible for the observed white frequency noise spectrum limiting the stability in the short-term region.

articleTitle: Coherence limits for very-long-baseline interferometry
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The quality of the frequency standards used in very-long-baseline interferometry limits the coherent integration time and the accuracy of geodetic experiments except in special cases when clock instabilities can be made to cancel out by using differential interferometry. Formulas are derived for estimating the coherence of these interferometers from the Allan variances of the frequency standards. Experiments using extremely high-quality frequency standards, such as hydrogen masers, may be limited by the phase noise that results from atmospheric and ionospheric fluctuations.

articleTitle: Capacitive transducer for accurate displacement control
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The underlying theory, design, and operation are presented for an interdigitated capacitive displacement transducer supported on an air-bearing stage. This device provides a purely electrical means of displacement measurement and offers the possibility of being closely matched to the substrate against thermal perturbations. Tests on a prototype system show the basic capacitive transducer to have a sensitivity of 2.6 mV/μm and a position uncertainty of 4 nm set by thermal noise.

articleTitle: Random testing of integrated circuits
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The paper concerns fault detection by applying a random input sequence simultaneously to a circuit under test and to a reference circuit. The objective is to determine the length of the input sequence to be applied, to obtain a given detection quality (detection probability). The paper gives a summary of the results which have been obtained for combined circuits, memories, SSI, and MSI sequential circuits.

articleTitle: A Wien-bridge oscillator with high-amplitude stability
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A FET-stabilized Wien-bridge oscillator, capable of maintaining an output voltage of 5 V to an accuracy of 0.02 percent with total harmonic distortion 0.01 percent is described. A linear model is presented for the amplitude-stabilizing control loop from which useful design relationships are developej.

articleTitle: Impedance of a loop surrounding a conducting cylinder
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The change in complex impedance between an ideal one-turn coil surrounding and coaxial with an infinitely long circular cylinder of conductivity δ and permeability μ and a similar coil without the core has been calculated. From the exact expression, a power series in the quantity δ/b (δ=skin depth; b=radius of core) has been developed. From this result, the change in impedance of a physically realistic multiturn coil can be estimated. The theory permits a rational approach to optimization of the design of eddy-current test coils and provides a possible means of detecting changes in the radius and conductivity of the cylinder.

articleTitle: A generalized method for de-embedding of multiport networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The concept of desegmentation proposed earlier for analysis of two-dimensional microwave circuits is used to evolve a generalized method for de-embedding of multiport devices (or networks). The formulation is in terms of 5-parameters of the embedded network and those of the embedding network. The proposed technique is illustrated by an example of three-port circuit.

articleTitle: Cepstral processing using spread spectra for cable diagnostics
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The use of Cepstrum (homomorphic deconvolution) processing simplifies cable discontinuity identification as compared to conventional time-domain reflectometry. Additionally, signal sources which approximate noise sources are fabricated and used; the use of signal sources whose spectral energies lie beyond the low-frequency power line harmonics permits minimization of a major interference contribution.

articleTitle: Network analysis by phase-modulated homodyne detection
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The network analyzer method using the homodyne detection principle and a sawtooth or stepped phase modulation can be generalized for an arbitrary phase-modulating function. The adjustment of the phase deviation of the modulated signal yields an exactly linear dependence between the phase of the microwave signal and the phase of the fundamental intermediate frequency signal at the mixer output.

articleTitle: A practical procedure for estimation of instantaneous frequency
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The instantaneous frequency of a frequency-modulated signal may be estimated using the zero crossings of the signal. Furthermore, the procedure is simple and gives good results when only samples of the signal are available and when the signal-to-noise ratio is above about 12 dB. An example is given.

articleTitle: Measurement principle of a reactive power meter for nonsinusoidal systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Presents a concept of the measurement of Budeanu reactive power in nonsinusoidal systems, based on the wideband π/2-phase-shift networks. An example of such a meter for a band of ten harmonics is given. The measurement error due to imperfections of the π/2-phase-shift networks is also analyzed.

articleTitle: Studies of magnetic field for transmitting and receiving loop antenna placed in a copiane
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A near-zone magnetic field generated by a small transmitting loop antenna has been used for the calibration of a radio receiver and a field intensity meter. In the calibration, the transmitting and receiving loops are sometimes located in a copiane with each other. In such a case, a theory to obtain magnetic-field strength is derived by using an infinite series. The errors due to treating the infinite series as a finite series and due to simplifying frequency terms are estimated. The applicable regions of the theory are shown as functions of loop spacing, loop radii, and wavelength. The differences between theoretical values and measured values were within ±0.1 dB at loop spacings of 25 to 60 cm for frequencies from 10 to 30 MHz.

articleTitle: Frequency dependence of 50-Ω coaxial open-circuit reflection standard
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The effective position of the open circuit in precision 7-mm 50-Ω coaxial transmission line is found experimentally to be located beyond the physical end of the center conductor by a distance 1.198 + 2.69 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−10</sup> f<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> millimeters at f megahertz (< 18 000). Because this determination is substantially identical to published theoretical values, the open circuit is recommended as a calibration standard for network analyzers.

articleTitle: A linear temperature-to-frequency converter using a thermistor
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A novel technique for output frequency linearization of a thermistor-astable multivibrator is presented. An analytical expression for the linearity condition is obtained and demonstrated experimentally. The astable multivibrator incorporating this technique is shown to offer an approximately linear temperature-to-frequency conversion in the range 0 to 86°C with a sensitivity of 21 Hz/°C. The experimental circuit exhibits excellent thermal stability for ambient temperature variations. The technique can also be used successfully in the lower temperature range −50 to 0°C.

articleTitle: Frequency stability of an oscillating maser: Analysis of the effect of an external feedback loop
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The noise temperature of the microwave cavity of an oscillating maser operated with an external feedback loop is given. The theoretical frequency stability of the signal delivered by the maser is deduced and the effect of the external feedback loop is discussed. Short- and mid-term frequency stabilities achievable with a conventional hydrogen maser with and without an external feedback loop and with a compact hydrogen maser operated either in active or in passive modes are given.

articleTitle: Condition for reflection coefficient magnitude greater than one for passive transmission line and passive load
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A simple, necessary condition is given for the magnitude of the reflection coefficient to be greater than unity for networks containing only passive elements.

articleTitle: A low-cost microprocessor-based Deep-Level Transient Spectroscopy (DLTS) system
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A microcomputer-based DLTS system is presented, in which the microcomputer functions as a signal averager and controller. The system can detect traps deeper than 0.20 eV from the band edges and 103 cm-3 less dense than the intentional dopant concentration. The system was applied to the study of deep traps in liquid-phase epitaxy (LPE) grown GaAs and vapor-phase epitaxy (VPE) grown GaAs0.75P0.25 light-emitting diodes (LEDs). A deep donor level at Ec -0.70 eV and σn=1.3×10-15 cm2 was found in the latter which agreed with capacitance-transients experiments done by another investigator. The electric-field strength was seen to inversely affect the electron capture cross section of this level. A minority-carrier trap reported at Ev+0.15 eV was observed but its energy level was not resolved due to its broad DLTS spectrum peak. The GaAs LED exhibited emission from a deep acceptor level at Eν+0.81 eV and σp=2.2×10-15 cm2, σn=6.8×10-22, and a deep donor level which could not be resolved.

articleTitle: Analytical and experimental approaches for the design of low-distortion Wien bridge oscillators
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Although Wien bridge oscillators are commonly used as fixed-frequency generators of low distortion there has apparently not been suggested a simple systematic method based on nonlinear theory for reducing their distortions. This paper attempts at filling the gap. This is achieved by suggesting a network which is on the one hand a Wien bridge oscillator and it can be also regarded as a Van der Pol oscillator. Van der Pol oscillators, however, are well known and as a result the task of systematically reducing the distortion becomes a straightforward procedure which is demonstrated by a series of experiments. Additional improvements (in the economy of design and with regard to a further reduction of distortions) are attained by slightly modifying the basic Van der Pol type system. The small level of distortion achieved in the present work systems is explained as partly due to the deliberate generation of harmonic components which are then subtracted from the output signal to remove the distortion components which are added by the amplifier circuit.

articleTitle: Range data entry techniques using a laser spot scanner and two linear solid-state image sensors
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: This paper proposes a three-dimensional (3-D) range-finding technique, using a laser spot scanner and two linear solid-state image sensors. Both the solid-state nature of image sensors and the avoidance of correspondence problem make it possible to obtain the range data of 3-D objects with high accuracy.

articleTitle: Ambiguity elimination in the measurement of permittivity with TE01n cylindrical cavities
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A technique to eliminate the ambiguity in the measurement of the electric permittivity with TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01n</inf> cylindrical cavities at microwave frequencies is described. The ambiguity is removed by introducing a new experimental parameter and the calculations are very simple. The theory, in the case of disc samples, is detailed. Measurements for some standard materials are presented.

articleTitle: New design aspects for an energetic particle telescope for space missions
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Describes new aspects which have been achieved in designing a charged particle dE/dx-E telescope to be flown on the International Solar Polar Mission. The instrument is designed to measure and resolve masses up to iron at energies above 100 keV per nucleon. Weight restrictions and radiation damage considerations led to new solutions for the overall system design and specific components. Beside radiation-resistant amplifiers, an analog-OR, a sample-and-hold circuit, and an extremely low power threshold discriminator have been developed. Power strobing of a fast ADC is another novel aspect of a `classical' measuring technique.

articleTitle: An inductorless all-pass phase-shifter configuration
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A new all-pass phase-shifter configuration using operational amplifier as an active element is described.

articleTitle: Effect of the worked layer in quartz-crystal plates on their frequency stabilities
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: This paper describes the direct measurement of the relation between the worked layers in quartz-crystal plates and their effect on the frequency stability. The rectangular fundamental 5-MHz A T-cut specimen plates lapped and polished with emery powder and cerium oxide, respectively, were placed in gap-type holders and connected with oscillator circuits, and their frequency stabilities were measured. The frequency stabilities are evaluated by the fractional frequency deviation to the nominal frequency ratio, power spectral density, and the Allan variance. The main results are: 1) The frequency drift due to the worked layer is dealt with as a relaxation process. It can be approximated by a sum of one to three terms of an exponential function. 2) The depth of the worked layer has a large effect not only on the long-term frequency stability but on the medium term in the Fourier frequency range of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup> to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−7</sup> Hz. 3) It does not have a dominant effect on the short-term stability with an averaging time of less than 10 s.

articleTitle: A simple microwave interferometer for measuring effective thickness of dielectric slabs
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A Michelson-type unequal path interferometer for measuring the effective thickness of dielectric slabs is presented. Due to unequal paths, this interferometer is frequency dependent so that frequency tuning of the source controls the phase difference between the two paths and serves as a phase shifter. FM modulation of the source enables determination of the null point with an electronic sensitivity of 0.02°. High spatial resolution (≃/2) is achieved by spacing a suitable horn antenna close to the dielectric surface. Detailed design considerations and experimental results concerning an X-band interferometer are presented.

articleTitle: Broad-band high-speed microwave power sensor using hot carriers in semiconductor
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The principal characteristics of a semiconductor power sensor based upon the temperature rise of hot carriers are investigated. A method of designing a broad-band coaxial mount is described. The hot-carrier power sensor is fabricated by a whisker contact to p-type germanium. A sensor using optimum resistivity results in a noise equivalent power of -58 dBm/Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup> with a 60-dB dynamic range. A broad-band-matched mount, having an average VSWR of 1.1:1 was attained for the frequency range from 1 to 12 GHz.

articleTitle: A SQUID magnetometer using a niobium thin-film microbridge
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A new type of Superconducting Quantum Interference Device (SQUID) using a submicrometer-width niobium thin-film microbridge on a sapphire substrate is described. This thin-film SQUID is suitable for mass production. It is mechanically rigid and resists mechanical shock and heat cycling. The SQUID is mounted in a niobium two-hole superconductive ring block to decrease its inductance, and an energy resolution of 5 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−29</sup> J/Hz is obtained. The paper also describes a magnetometer (comprising this SQUIÜ and gradiometer-type search coils) as well as a magnetically shielded room used to measure magnetocardiograms.

articleTitle: A microwave bridge method for measuring the complex permittivity of liquids
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: In this short paper, a microwave bridge method is discussed for measuring the complex permittivity of dielectric materials. The underlying principle of the technique along with the experimental results is presented here. The complex permittivities of benzene, carbon tetrachloride, petrol, and kerosene are illustrated at a few frequencies in X-band. The variation of the dielectric properties of petrol-kerosene mixture is also studied by this method.

articleTitle: A new approach to digital frequency synthesis
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: This paper presents a new technique of synthesizing frequencies in steps of 1 Hz from 1 to 399999 Hz. The synthesized waveform is a symmetrical square wave and transistor-transistor logic (TTL) compatible. The algorithm used for the synthesis allows for very efficient use of digital implementation of the system. The complete system consists of an input device, a BCD/binary converter, a binary divider, a digital comparator, and a phase-locked loop (PLL) frequency multiplier.

articleTitle: Intermodulation measurement using a microcomputer
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: An intermodulation distortion measurement technique using a microcomputer is studied. This approach is based on the theory deduced via a stochastic method instead of a series technique; it is also useful for nonlinear amplifiers that do not have smooth characteristics, such as a piecewise-linear limiter, a class-C amplifier, an A-D converter, etc.... This technique also allows to measure the intermodulation of amplifiers whose characteristics are temperature dependent. Measurement errors associated with the A-D conversion in the equipment are also discussed and the accuracy of this method is confirmed experimentally by using a UHF transistor amplifier.

articleTitle: CMRR performance limits of analog multiplexers using normal-mode filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: An analysis of the common-mode rejection (CMR) of low-level analog multiplexers using normal-mode filters is presented. The CMR is shown to be limited by the multiplexer bus capacitance. Simple analytical expressions are presented for predicting the CMR performance of these multiplexers.

articleTitle: A model for 1/f noise
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: As in many other fields, 1/f noise plays an important role in precise electromagnetic measurements. Starting from the assumption that noise is generated by fluctuations of a parameter, subject to a diffusion equation, a model is developed which for samples of finite size produces a 1/f spectrum over a wide frequency range.

articleTitle: A direct-reading instrument for measurements of inductance and Q of ferrite core coils
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A resonant circuit consisting of a coil to be tested and two capacitors in series, one of which is fixed and the other variable, is used to permit the direct readings of the inductance and Q by prototype instrument was built that could measure the inductance from 200 to 400 μH and Q values up to 400 at 796 kHz.

articleTitle: Use of vacuum tubes in test instrumentation for measuring characteristics of fast high-voltage semiconductor devices
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Circuits are described that permit measurement of fast events occurring in power semiconductors. These circuits were developed for the dynamic characterization of transistors used in inductive-load switching applications. Fast voltage clamping using vacuum diodes is discussed, and reference is made to a unique circuit that was built for performing nondestructive, reverse-bias, second-breakdown tests on transistors.

articleTitle: Microprocessor-controlled acquisition system for the determination of MOS transistor parameters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Discusses a microprocessor-controlled data acquisition system for automated acquisition of MOS transistor parameters. The Analog Signal Processor and the Control Interface Circuit are described. Finally, the authors explain the procedure of parameter determination based on the least squares estimation criterion. This procedure is applied to long-channel, surface-channel, enhancement-mode PMOS transistors. The ID-VD curves exhibit an accuracy of 1-3 percent compared with the experimental characteristics.

articleTitle: Single shunt fault diagnosis in a resistive ladder
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The problem of locating a single shunt fault in a uniform resistive ladder network is considered. A simple method, based on resistance measurements is proposed for the case where the total number of nodes is small and all of them are accessible. Two strategies are discussed for reducing the number of measurements when the number of nodes is large but all nodes are still accessible. When internal nodes are not accessible, it is shown that in theory, it is possible to locate the fault from two resistance measurements at the ports. However, when the number of nodes is large, and the fault is well inside the ladder, such a method is susceptible to large errors. Experimental results are given for some representative ladders.

articleTitle: Dynamics of the heterodyne spectrum analyzer with rectangular bandpass filter
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Mathematical model of the dynamic frequency characteristics of the heterodyne spectrum analyzer with a rectangular bandpass filter of small relative bandwidth is constructed. The model is investigated numerically and proved experimentally.

articleTitle: A simple technique for precise voltage control of oscillator frequencies
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A proportional feedback control scheme is proposed to obtain a precise linear relationship between the control voltage and the frequency of oscillators. Experimental results agree closely with the theory. The scheme is simple in circuitry, versatile, and suitable for mass production.

articleTitle: Clock synchronization experiment via SYMPHONIE satellite
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Clock synchronization experiment between ground stations in Beijing and Shanghai and also between Nanjing and Shanghai were carried out in March, 1979, by the National Institute of Metrology of China. Based on the results of this experiment, two Cs-atomic clocks, one located in Raisting (Federal Republic of Germany) and the other in Nanjing (China) were compared from June 18 to 27,1979, via SYMPHONIE satellite using two-way relay noncoherent time-transfer technique. The experiment was jointly sponsored by the National Institute of Metrology of China (NIM) and the Physikalisch Technische Bundesanstalt (PTB). The experimental results showed that an accuracy of 80 ns was achieved for the clock synchronization with a random fluctuation of about 10 ns. These results were confirmed by the use of a portable clock.

articleTitle: A programmable LF voltage ratio transformer using CMOS switches
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A programmable 12-bit voltage ratio device having a voltage rating of 0.1 times frequency and a terminal linearity error of less than 1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−7</sup> at 10–80 Hz is described. The compact design incorporates a 3-stage ratio transformer and it accommodates the use of solid-state switches having an ON-resistance of 100 Ω.

articleTitle: The determination of the scattering parameters of microwave TV-port networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: It is shown that the solution of a linear system of equations permits the determination of all scattering parameters of an n-port microwave structure with the aid of a resonance technique based on transmission and length measurements and a nonresonance procedure based on reflection coefficient measurements. The resonance method is primarily intended for lossless networks but its extension to lossy networks is discussed.

articleTitle: A decade range linearly tunable versatile filter
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A modified version of the Kerwin-Huelsman-Newcomb biquad is presented which is electronically tunable almost linearly over a decade range of center frequency. The circuit is suitable for use as a tunable universal filtering module and can be easily digitally programmed.

articleTitle: An active frequency meter
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: This short paper deals with the theory and fabrication of a new frequency meter, which is used for the measurement of frequency in the range from a few hertz to 100 kHz. It is a frequency-selective bridge and is made of discrete passive R and C components and an integrated operational amplifier. At bridge balance, the frequency under measurement is given in terms of the values of resistors and capacitors only. Advantages, limitations, and sources of errors of the frequency meter are discussed. The theory is experimentally verified.

articleTitle: A cascade phase-sensitive detector: II — Phase filter synthesis
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: For pt.I see ibid., no.1, p.3-6 (March 1980). A synthesis procedure of the phase filter is described. The procedure consists of the Fourier-series approximation= of the specified transfer function and the mechanization of each term in the series by means of the cascadable phase-sensitive detectors (CPSDs). The prototype filter implemented by four-stage CPSD confirms the procedure. The effect of input noise on the transfer function is analyzed to show that the signal-to-noise power ratio higher than 7.7 dB is necessary for the satisfactory operation of the fifth-order filter.

articleTitle: On estimation of noise variance in the presence of a narrow-band signal
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The procedure for noise variance estimation in the presence of a narrow-band signal with a priori unknown parameters is discussed. The fast suppression of a narrow-band signal prior to measurement of a noise variance is accomplished with a low-order Adaptive Notch Filter (ANF) based on a linear prediction. It is shown that a good estimation of noise variance can be obtained over the time-limited interval in spite of the presence of a strong narrow-band signal. Computer simulation results which demonstrate the proposed algorithm performance are included.

articleTitle: A high-frequency Kerr-effect microscope for bubble devices
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A Kerr-effect microscope is described which has been assembled specifically for studies of the dynamic magnetization of the Permalloy elements of magnetic-bubble memory devices at frequencies up to 300 kHz with an illumination spot size of approximately 2 μm. Procedures are described for the setting up and alignment of the microscope and for the calibration of the rotating field.

articleTitle: Guarding techniques for resistance thermometers
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Theoretical and practical aspects of the application of electrical guards to resistance thermometers are discussed, with a view toward suppressing errors caused by imperfect electrical insulation at high temperatures. Some simple techniques for modifying existing resistance thermometer bridges are described.

articleTitle: Receiver design for laser ranging to satellites
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The paper provides a quantitative basis for receiver design whereby timing performance can be evaluated for an arbitrary impulse response using known or measurable system parameters. The analysis accounts for the statistical independence of the multiplication processes of the dynodes as well as the possibility of their non-Poisson behavior. Fixed threshold, constant fraction, and median receivers have been analyzed, and the median receiver has been shown to be significantly superior. Experimental results have been presented which show reasonable agreement with the theory and which confirm the superiority of median timing.

articleTitle: A dipole detuning technique for proximity and thickness measurements
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Experimental results are presented which demonstrate that both the magnitude and phase of the input reflection coefficient of a dipole placed near a conducting plane are sensitive monotonie functions of the dipole-to-plane separation. Measurement applications which exploit this characteristic are suggested.

articleTitle: Deconvolution as a feasible alternative to the root-sum-squares rule for non-Gaussian transition duration analysis
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A 100-ps Debye line filter is analyzed for transition duration using both deconvolution and root-sum-squares methods. The latter method shows errors of ±12 percent for the cases presented, while deconvolution agrees to within 0.3 percent of the theoretical filter model. In addition, the deconvoluted Debye filter waveform matches the theoretical step response to within less than 1 percent at all points in a 500-ps time epoch.

articleTitle: Microprocessor-controlled drill analyzer
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A microprocessor-controlled instrument was developed for automatic measurement of drill geometry. The position of a reciprocating stylus is measured upon contact with the sample via an analog-digital converter and a linear variable differential transformer (LVDT). Either a guarded stereo phono cartridge or an electrical contact stylus senses contact. Output data are digital readouts plus analog plots. Plots are either polar plots of equal height contours, height versus angle for fixed radius or height, or departures from conical versus position. The sources of error are discussed; achievable accuracy of height measurements is approximately ±1 percent ±25 μm.

articleTitle: An autoranging voltmeter circuit without range resistors
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: An autoranging circuit for digital voltmeter without range resistors is presented. The circuit uses a microprocessor-based time-averaging technique. This technique can achieve an accuracy comparable to a 4½ digit DVM in 5-decade range. An autozero and autopolarity circuit is also presented.

articleTitle: A study on the static calibration of a hot wire
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: It is shown that the method of nonlinear regression is more suitable in the determination of the parameters of the static calibration of a hot wire. The method has a distinct advantage that the exponent n is independent of flow velocity.

articleTitle: A variable-threshold digitizer for photodiode arrays
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: It was observed that the output amplifier of a photodiode array was not accurately representing the expected output from a known picture. Consequently, fixed-threshold digitizer proved unsatisfactory. This paper suggests a variable-threshold digitizer to improve performance.

articleTitle: Fixed cross coils and moving magnet-type temperature indicator
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A temperature indicator is described which is essentially composed of a pair of fixed cross coils and a movable permanent magnet with a pointer and used together with an IC amplifier. Static and dynamic indication characteristics are theoretically analyzed and compared with the experimental data.

articleTitle: A high-quality digital filter instrument
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A high-quality real-time low power dissipation 12-bit low-pass digital-filter instrument is described. It is a hardware version of a recently proposed multirate ladder structure which can be implemented entirely without digital multipliers. The frequency response of the filter is user programmable and is determined by an operating sequence stored in a read-only memory. A numerical technique is described for determining the operating sequence corresponding to a particular low-pass response. Measured frequency responses are shown for four different cutoff frequencies between 2 and 5.5 kHz) for the fifth-order filter instrument.

articleTitle: AC ripple and DC error in RMS-to-DC converters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The differential equation describing the operation of explicit and implicit rms-to-dc converters is solved and the solution is used to calculate the magnitude of the second-harmonic component and of the dc error at the output of these devices. The results obtained are identical to estimates made using approximate superposition techniques.

articleTitle: A digital profiler for the characterization of semiconductors
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Describes an automatic digital profiler which measures the density of free carriers versus depth in a semiconductor material. The instrument is controlled by a microprocessor in order to reduce operator intervention and eliminate some of the errors inherent in analog systems.

articleTitle: A new 2-kV common-mode voltage wide-band isolation amplifier
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Describes a new modulation-demodulation technique for isolation amplifiers, particularly useful for multichannel data acquisition systems. Input and output stages are transformer coupled using an improved version of the amplitude-modulation technique of a symmetric square wave, which requires a simple rectifier bridge for demodulation. Characteristics of the isolation stage obtained in this way are excellent linearity and gain stability, typical of magnetic coupling, and a frequency bandwidth ranging from DC to an upper limit which, at least in principle, is not fixed by the demodulation technique; moreover, common-mode voltages in the kilovolt range are obtainable. Details of an amplifier are given, designed as the analog input stage of a multichannel data acquisition system.

articleTitle: Measurement method for the large-signal admittance of mounted IMPATT diodes
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The procedure employs a network analyzer and a computer optimization routine. An error network is introduced to account for drift of the measurement system and a second network is used to account for the mounted-diode parasitics. The measurement method is rapid and accurate, and is especially suitable when measurements are required at several frequencies. Typical large-signal admittance results, obtained for a Si IMPATT diode at several frequencies, are presented.

articleTitle: A method to increase the accuracy of fast Fourier transform calculations for rapidly varying functions
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The calculation may be improved by subtracting beforehand a convenient auxiliary function, chosen in such a manner that the representative curve resulting from the subtraction exhibits only smooth variations.

articleTitle: A new system for measuring low DC currents
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A new system for measuring low dc current covering a wide range of currents is presented. It eliminates the need of switches in the circuit where the measured current flows. The system design simplifies the ranging problem and paves the way for easier development of instrumentation where low dc currents should be measured.

articleTitle: The transient response of a sampling oscillographic system excited by a step-like pulse having overshoot
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The transient response of a sampling oscillographic system with linear gating diodes excited by a theoretical step-like pulse possessing overshoot is analyzed. Expressions for the transient function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h(\bar {t})$</tex> of the excited system, the first 0–100-percent transition duration for the first crossing of the final value (100-percent) level <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar {t}_T$</tex>, and the overshoot <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar \delta$</tex> are derived. It is shown that the relationship between the overshoot <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar \delta$</tex> of the excited system response and the overshoot δ of the step-like input pulse is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar \delta = n \delta^2$</tex>. An example of the response has been generated by computer simulation, and the overshoot relation has been compared to experimental data. The results of this work are useful in estimating the effects of overshoot in the calibration of sampling oscilloscopes and high-speed pulses.

articleTitle: Design for automated testing of analog data channels in a PCM switching system
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Semi-automatic suboptimal tests of analog data channels in a time-multiplexed pulse-code modulation (PCM) digital switching system are presented. The intent of the approach used was to provide a computer-controlled go, no-go testing capability for the analog I/O channels of the switch. Interplay between hardware design constraints and desired testability features are discussed. Results of maintainability demonstration tests were satisfying. Methods for improving the capabilities of this approach (i.e., provision of optimal characteristics) are readily available.

articleTitle: An improvement to an analog-to-digital converter for differential transducers
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: An improvement to a paper recently published in this journal is described. The original paper shows how a quantity, measured by a pair of differential resistive transducers, can be converted into a time interval by incorporating the transducers in the integrator of a dual-slope analog-to-digital converter. Offset error is measured by using two dual-slope cycles. The improvement shows how the calculation of the offset can be avoided if the reference time of one of the dual-slope cycles is modified in accordance with previous measurements.

articleTitle: Computer-controlled scattering measurements in a parallel-plate configuration
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: This paper describes an instrument developed for the purpose of studying the propagation of microwaves through and scattered by objects of varying dielectric properties. Ultimately, it is hoped that a map of the internal electromagnetic structure of the object can be reconstructed from the measurement of the amplitude and/or the phase of the fields outside the object. For this purpose, the field must be sampled at a large number of points; this is done under computer control using a minicomputer. The geometry of the problem is simplified by performing the measurements in a parallel-plate configuration. The minicomputer controls the data acquisition, storage of the data, and data display. This paper includes a description of the hardware and software components of the system and then illustrates its performance with measured distributions for some object geometries.

articleTitle: Digital Q measurement of audio-frequency inductors
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A measurement technique which enables precise digital readout of the quality factor Q of audio-frequency inductors is presented. It employs a switched capacitor C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf> to obtain a negative conductance whose magnitude G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf> is directly proportional to the switching frequency f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>. This variable negative conductance is connected across a parallel resonant circuit consisting of the inductor under test and a capacitor C. The switching frequency is slowly increased and the loss in the circuit is reduced until the tuned circuit starts oscillating at the resonant frequency f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. The quality factor Q of the coil at the frequency f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is given by Q = 2π(C/C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>)(f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>/f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>). Since the frequency ratio can be determined to a high degree of precision, the accuracy of the Q measurement is governed by the precision of (C/C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>). The instrument design and experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: A comparison of Elmore and traditional rise times
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A comparison is made of Elmore and traditional rise times for a cascaded linear network. It is shown that the customary application of the square-law relationship, derived by Elmore, to traditional rise time evaluations leads to a significant error.

articleTitle: Multichannel digital ventilated psychrometer using eight-bit microcomputer
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A multichannel digital ventilated psychrometer using an 8-bit microcomputer has been developed. It offers the advantages of direct reading of the relative humidity (RH) and the temperature from the digital indicator (or the CRT indicator) as well as multichannel use. The sensing of humidity is based on the psychrometric principle by two integrated circuit (IC) temperature transducers acting as dry and wet bulbs. The temperature of the dry bulb has a range of 0–50°C with a linearity better than 0.05°C. The temperatures of the dry and wet bulbs are converted into proportional voltages which are fed into a microcomputer after having been converted into digital form by the A/D converter. As the RH data for dry-bulb temperature and dry- and wet-bulb temperature difference have previously been stored in the memory, the corresponding RH data can be derived from using the necessary steps of the program. The results are displayed on a digital indicator. The indication shows the channel number being measured, the RH, and the dry-bulb temperature. The experimental results show that it is possible to make an apparatus to give a direct indication of RH for the multiple sensors and the accuracy of the apparatus is estimated to contain an RH error of less than 2 percent with a response time of less than 20 s. It may be used both for measurement and control of a multiple humidity environment.

articleTitle: On the maximum of the spectral density of the amplitude fluctuations of a maser oscillator
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The spectral density of the amplitude fluctuations of a maser oscillator shows a peak when the saturation factor is high enough. This correspondence gives an analytical expression for the Fourier frequency at which the maximum arises, in terms of the saturation factor and the transverse and longitudinal relaxation time constants.

articleTitle: A new method for optimum alignment of digital communications equipment
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The technique is to perform final adjustments on the equipment while monitoring the bit error rate at a very low signal-to-Gaussian noise ratio. Experimental verification of the method is presented.

articleTitle: SNR analysis of log companding for use in a digital recording/data analysis system
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: This paper presents an SNR analysis of a bilateral log compandor that was used in a portable wide-bandwidth digital recording system designed to generate field recordings of wide-band atmospheric noise in the MF radio spectrum [1], [2]. Log-compression amplifiers are used in the I and Q channels of the recorder receiver function to compress dynamic range from 120 to about 50 dB. Following A/D conversion, the compressed I and Q channel signals are digitally recorded on magnetic tape. The recorded data are then transcribed onto magnetic computer tape for subsequent data analysis. Inverse log compression of the transcribed samples is accomplished via a software log-expansion algorithm exactly matched to the inverse characteristics of each of the I and Q channel log-compression amplifiers. The present analysis shows that samples of the I and Q channel signals can be generated from samples of the log-compressed signals by inverse log compression without concern for aliasing error. A measure of the accuracy of the resulting sampled sequence is then developed analytically in closed form in terms of an SNR measure for the decompressed samples.

articleTitle: Phase-coherent synthesis and precision frequency measurements in the far infrared
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A short review of the basic concepts and problems in frequency multiplication into the infrared region of the electromagnetic spectrum is given. Results obtained with a multiplier chain starting from 5 MHz are reported. The carrier collapse is found at a frequency of about 15 THz. The present state of technological development is illustrated and the inherent limitations of this technique are indicated. The need for more spectral pure sources than those now available and/or different approaches is underlined in connection with the increasing thrust towards the measurement of visible frequencies.

articleTitle: Microprocessors simplify humidity measurements
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Wet-bulb and dry-bulb thermistors are interfaced directly with a microprocessor without the need for a separate A/D converter or other complex analog signal conditioning circuitry to provide a simple and reliable yet flexible and cost-effective approach to measuring humidity. Two such circuits are described along with the digital signal processing algorithms that help extend the range and linearize the response of the sensors. With the first approach, the thermistors become part of a dual resistor-controlled-oscillator circuit; oscillator frequencies are mapped into dry-bulb and wet-bulb temperatures. For the second approach, the thermistors reside in a pul-sewidth-modulation circuit; pulsewidths are mapped into dry-bulb and wet-bulb temperatures. The transfer function and sensitivity coefficients for each circuit are calculated. Overall measurement system accuracy is limited by the uncertainties in the wet-bulb and dry-bulb sensors and not by thermal drift, component aging, variations in power supply voltages, or nonlinearities in other circuit components.

articleTitle: A computer system for analysis of high capacity components in optical-fiber links
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The system includes an HP 21MX minicomputer with a 32K main memory and a disk, making it possible to handle easily 4096 data points in both the time and the frequency domains. The modular organization of the software and the command file control of the processing have created a flexible system that has proved to be useful in evaluating models of semiconductor lasers and avalanche photodiodes. Furthermore, the system has been used to develop modulation methods for semiconductor lasers in the gigabit per second range.

articleTitle: The double dual-slope multiplier: Elimination of offset
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The double dual-slope multiplier is a multiplying analog-to-digital converter based on the dual-slope integrating converter. The ratio of the product of two unknown voltages to the square of a reference voltage is obtained in terms of the ratio of a measured time interval to a known time interval. Offset errors, which are the main source of error, are described and a modification which greatly reduces the error is proposed. The errors consist of scale factor, output, and linear feedthrough errors. The scale factor and output errors can be measured by a cycle consisting of two dual-slope measurements that use the reference voltage only. The feedthrough errors can be eliminated if the multiplying cycle is repeated with the order of the inputs reversed. The operation of the multiplier when the inputs are less than the offset is considered in detail. Since the decision making, memory, and calculations necessary for the control of the multiplier and the correction of the offset are considerable, the method is mainly applicable to precision instruments equipped with a microprocessor.

articleTitle: On manuscript submission, processing, review, and publication
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: THERE HAVE BEEN several publications on peer review in the IEEE Spectrum (August and September 1981) and in Physics Today (January and June 1981). The subject is of interest to both authors and editors. Very often the procedure of manuscript processing and review is not well understood. This is because the procedures as well as the review are not objective enough and, in fact, may be highly subjective depending on one's point of view. Although certain procedures can be standardized, they are mechanical in nature and do not affect the outcome.

articleTitle: Author index
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: This index covers all technical items - papers, correspondence, reviews, etc. - that appeared in this periodical during the year, and items from previous years that were commented upon or corrected in this year. Departments and other items may also be covered if they have been judged to have archival value. The Author Index contains the primary entry for each item, listed under the first author's name. The primary entry includes the co-authors' names, the title of the paper or other item, and its location, specified by the publication abbreviation, year, month, and inclusive pagination. The Subject Index contains entries describing the item under all appropriate subject headings, plus the first author's name, the publication abbreviation, month, and year, and inclusive pages. Note that the item title is found only under the primary entry in the Author Index.

abstract: THE RECOGNITION of personal achievements by one's peers is one of the most satisfying elements of a professional career. Election to the grade of Fellow within the IEEE is one of the honors that is a possibility for every Senior Member. Of even greater honor is being nominated and chosen as the recipient of one of the IEEE Field Awards which, for those whose activity is instrumentation and measurement, implies the Morris E. Leeds Award for “outstanding contribution in the field of electrical measurement.”
